title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Delete the overload you pointed at
summary: With two dead overloads in one file, the quick fix offered on the second one deleted the first. The action found its finding by name, and a name is shared by every overload.

highlights.title: The lightbulb acts on the line under the cursor
highlights.description: The declaration under the cursor was already resolved on the current text, but the finding attached to it was picked by name, so the first overload won every time.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Deleting an unused declaration removes the one the cursor sits on. With two dead overloads of the same name in a file, the fix offered on the second removed the first instead, along with whatever annotation it carried.
The title and the verdict shown in the lightbulb came from that same wrong finding, so the second overload could be offered the action meant for the first.
This path opened in 1.42.63, which started reporting two dead homonyms declared in one file. The removal itself was already fixed in 1.42.65; this is the step just above it.
